the hemicholinum ether analogues, which are more active than the parent compound, hemicholinium (HC-3), as inhibitors of ACH synthesis by non-depolarized brain minces (in vitro) are less active than HC3 as inhibitors of the Ca-dependent release of ACh by K-depolarization of brain minces (also in vitro).

HC-3 and its ether analogues, which are more active than HC3 as inhibitors of choline acetylase and cholinergic contractions, are significantly less active than the parent compound as inhibitors of ACH synthesis in K-depolarization, suggesting that the primary site of action of HC-1 on ACh synthesis is not at the active site of choline acylase but rather is at a site involved in the synthesis of choline from phosphatidyl choline.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

HC-3 and the hemicholinum acetals are effective and selective inhibitors of choline uptake by cholinergic nerve terminals, and that the hemicholinums are not effective inhibitors of choline acetylase or cholinesterases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the hemicholinia acetals and the seco tautomers are equipotent to HC3 as inhibitors of the synthesis of acetycholine by mouse-brain (in vitro), but only 1-2 times as effective as inhibitors of the release of ACh induced by potassium depolarization.

the hemiacetal and DMAE derivatives of HC-3 are more potent than HC-3 in inhibiting ACh synthesis in K-depolarizing conditions and are more potent as postjunctional blockers of ACh-induced contraction of the frog rectal muscle.

the ether analogues of HC-3 are equipotent to the parent compound as inhibitors of ACH synthesis by non-depolarized minces, but are only 1/2 to 1/3 so active as inhibitors of the K-evoked release of newly-formed ACh from depolarized minces.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the active moiety of hemicholinium is the hemiacetal form of hemicholinuim-3 and not the seco form.
the hemicholinum acetals and DMAA have a greater inhibitory effect than HC-3 on cholinergic nerve terminals, and that this effect is more potent in depolarized preparations.
the ether analogues of HC-3 are more potent inhibitors of acetylcholinesterase than HC-3 itself and that they have a much greater effect on the synthesis of ACh by non-depolaized mouse brain mince.
